snippet.title: Texas county emergency management official says he was asleep during deadly flood
snippet.description:
For the first time since catastrophic flooding killed more than 100 people in Kerr County, Texas, the county emergency management director conceded that he was sick and asleep as the water rose to historic levels on the Guadalupe River.

William "Dub" Thomas, the Kerr County emergency management director since 2015, detailed his whereabouts during the crisis to the Texas House and Senate Select Committees on Disaster Preparedness and Flooding on Thursday in Kerrville, Texas.

snippet.title: 13 Walmart Items Preppers Are Quietly Buying Before November 5 (All Under $2!)
snippet.description:
❄️ 13 WALMART Items to Buy Before November 5th | Cheap Winter Emergency Supplies!

Can you prepare for winter power outages, freezing temperatures, and unexpected emergencies for under $30 at Walmart? Discover 13 affordable Walmart items that could make a real difference when the lights go out, the temperature drops, or a winter storm catches your household off guard.

Most of these cheap emergency preparedness supplies cost less than $2 each, and every item on this list costs less than $5 based on the Walmart prices featured in the video.

With daylight saving time ending on November 1, 2026, darker evenings and colder weather are approaching. Now is a practical time to check your emergency supplies before winter weather arrives.

In this Homestead Roots video, we're revealing 13 inexpensive Walmart survival essentials, from emergency rain protection and hand warmers to backup lighting, shelf-stable food, drinking water, and one surprisingly important 97-cent item almost everyone overlooks.

Stay until #1 — it could become essential when your phone battery dies!


🏡 WHY PREPARE BEFORE NOVEMBER 5TH?

Winter emergencies aren't always dramatic blizzards.

Sometimes they're ordinary problems:

⚡ A power outage after sunset
🌧️ Cold rain soaking your clothes
🚗 A vehicle stranded on an icy road
🚰 A frozen pipe interrupting water service
🔦 A flashlight with dead batteries
📱 A phone that dies when you need an important number
🥶 A cold house with no working furnace

The best emergency supplies are the ones you can actually find, reach, and use when they're needed.

🔦 CHEAP POWER OUTAGE PREPAREDNESS TIPS

✅ Keep a working flashlight or headlamp near each bed.
✅ Store extra batteries with your emergency lights.
✅ Keep emergency blankets and warm clothing accessible.
✅ Store at least one gallon of water per person per day.
✅ Maintain foods that are simple to prepare.
✅ Keep a written list of emergency phone numbers.
✅ Test equipment before the first winter storm.
✅ Build your emergency kit gradually instead of panic buying.

📓 WHAT SHOULD GO IN YOUR EMERGENCY NOTEBOOK?

Write down family phone numbers, trusted neighbors, medical contacts, medication information, utility outage numbers, insurance details, and your household's emergency meeting place.

Store the notebook in a waterproof bag with a pen and pencil.

A digital backup is useful, but a paper copy doesn't need electricity.

🌾 ABOUT HOMESTEAD ROOTS

At Homestead Roots, we explore affordable emergency preparedness, traditional self-reliance, winter survival, practical homesteading, food storage, and everyday skills that help families become more prepared.

You don't need expensive survival equipment to start. Sometimes preparation begins with a few ordinary supplies from the grocery or hardware aisle.

🔔 SUBSCRIBE for weekly videos about budget prepping, Walmart survival supplies, winter preparedness, homesteading, and power outage essentials.

💬 JOIN THE CONVERSATION!

Which THREE of these 13 Walmart items are missing from your emergency kit?

And what's the very first thing you would write in your emergency notebook?

👇 Share your answer in the comments!

👍 LIKE this video if you found it useful.
🔔 SUBSCRIBE to Homestead Roots.
📤 SHARE with someone building a winter emergency kit on a budget.

⚠️ SAFETY NOTES

Prices and product availability vary by store and may change. Never use candles or portable fuel-burning cooking equipment as indoor heating sources. Keep flames away from combustible materials and never leave them unattended. Hand warmers can cause burns if misused. Reflective blankets are supplemental protection, not a substitute for adequate winter shelter and clothing.

If you suspect hypothermia, carbon monoxide exposure, or another medical emergency, seek immediate assistance.

snippet.title: These 8 Items Are USELESS After an EMP — Stop Stockpiling Them
snippet.description:
#PrepperPantry #Stockpile #FoodShortage2026
You've spent months — maybe years — building a stockpile you trust. But if an electromagnetic pulse event hits, eight of the most commonly hoarded items in the prepper community become instant dead weight. Not damaged. Not degraded. Completely, permanently useless.
The problem isn't that people don't take EMPs seriously. The problem is they prep for EMPs the same way they prep for everything else — and an EMP isn't everything else. It doesn't disrupt supply chains. It doesn't cause shortages. It kills functionality at the component level. Circuits. Chips. Capacitors. Anything with a microprocessor built after a certain year becomes a brick. And that threshold includes items most preppers consider analog, mechanical, or "simple enough" to survive.
Here's where it gets uncomfortable. Some of the most expensive items in your entire prep — things you researched, compared, and specifically chose because they seemed like smart long-term investments — have the same vulnerability as a smartphone sitting on your kitchen counter. They just don't look like they do. One item on this list is recommended by nearly every major prepper channel on this platform. It shows up in starter kits, bug-out bags, and Amazon prep lists everywhere. And it will not function for a single second after an EMP. Not one.
This video isn't about fear. It's about redirect. Every dollar locked into a post-EMP paperweight is a dollar that should've gone toward an analog alternative that actually works when the grid doesn't just go down — it doesn't come back.
Stop storing what won't work. Start replacing it with what will.

snippet.title: Help Us Pass the Amateur Radio Emergency Preparedness Act
snippet.description:
ARRL has launched a nationwide grassroots campaign aimed at securing the passage of federal legislation that would grant Amateur Radio Operators the same rights to install antennas on their property as those enjoyed by users of TV antennas, wireless internet, and flagpoles.

The campaign follows the reintroduction of the Amateur Radio Emergency Preparedness Act in February 2025. The bipartisan bills -- H.R.1094 in the House and S.459 in the Senate -- are designed to prevent restrictive homeowners’ association (HOA) rules that currently prohibit or severely limit the installation of amateur radio antennas, even when such antennas are hidden in trees, placed in attics, mounted on vehicles, or look like flagpoles.

snippet.title: Air Fryer Chicken Fajita Bowls | High-Protein Meal Prep #highprotein #cooking
snippet.description:
Tired of complicated meal prep? These Air Fryer Chicken Fajita Bowls are an easy high-protein meal made with seasoned chicken, four colorful bell peppers, red onion, rice, and fresh lime.

Makes 4 Servings

Per Serving:
Calories: ~575
Protein: ~55g
Carbohydrates: ~65g
Fat: ~10g

Ingredients:

* 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, diced
* 1 red bell pepper, diced
* 1 yellow bell pepper, diced
* 1 orange bell pepper, diced
* 1 green bell pepper, diced
* 1 medium red onion, diced
* 2 packets fajita seasoning
* 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
* Cooking spray
* 1⅓ cups (250g) dry white rice
* 1⅔ cups water

Instructions:
Dice the chicken, bell peppers, and red onion. Add everything to a large bowl with the fajita seasoning and lime juice and toss until evenly coated. Lightly spray the air fryer basket and air fry at 400°F for 14–16 minutes, tossing halfway through, until the chicken reaches 165°F internally. Cook the rice separately, then divide the rice and chicken fajita mixture evenly between 4 meal prep containers.
